notes: external.inspire_experiment is null: INSPIRE was not consulted (its rate budget belongs to the supervised importer).
The CYGNUS proto-collaboration (a proposed multi-site network of directional TPCs) is not recorded as an experiment: it has no fixed host site, no approval and no results (see the log).
No reachable official CYGNO or INITIUM website was found (web.infn.it/cygno returned 404 on 2026-10-26); links.website stays null.
CYGNO-04 is in Hall F of LNGS, which has no site record; the LNGS Hall B site (the facility's primary site, the same approximate coordinate as halls A and C) is referenced.
The CYGNO collaboration has published detector R&D and background studies with the LIME prototype but, in the sources read, no dark matter exclusion limit.

physics_goals.quote: The CYGNO experiment (a CYGNus module with Optical readout) aims to exploit the optical readout approach of multiple-GEM structures in large volume TPCs for the study of rare events as interactions of low-mass DM or solar neutrinos.
physics_goals.value: Directional search for low-mass WIMP dark matter with an optically read out gas TPC

summary.plain: CYGNO is a directional dark matter project at Gran Sasso. A gas chamber of helium and CF4 turns particle tracks into light that cameras photograph, giving 3D tracks and their direction. A 50-litre prototype ran underground; a 0.4 cubic-metre demonstrator is being built.
summary.technical: CYGNus module with Optical readout: He:CF4 (60:40) atmospheric-pressure TPC with triple-GEM amplification and optical readout (sCMOS camera for X-Y, PMTs for the drift coordinate). PHASE 0: 50 L LIME prototype, commissioned overground at LNF and installed underground at LNGS in February 2022 (about 27 months of data in five shielding configurations). PHASE 1: CYGNO-04, a 0.4 m^3 back-to-back TPC in LNGS Hall F, under construction; PHASE 2 aims at O(30) m^3. Part of the CYGNUS proto-collaboration; INITIUM ERC grant.
